result.title: Signs of Wear: Evaluating Intelligent Speed Assistance Under Synthetic Adverse Conditions
result.summary: Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) systems rely on cameras to recognize speed-limit signs, yet existing benchmarks underrepresent the weathered, dirty, and overgrown signs commonly encountered on rural roads. We use generative image editing to introduce different forms of wear into real street-level images of speed-limit signs. The resulting ISA-Wear dataset contains paired original and edited images. Guided by text instructions, a multimodal image-editing model adds snow, rust, vegetation, faded paint, or mud to the speed-limit sign in a street-level frame at three severity levels. Where appropriate, the surrounding scene is adapted as well, and the viewpoint is kept. Every edited frame has an unedited counterpart, and we only evaluate frames whose original is recognized correctly, so any failure can be attributed to the wear. Since the model alters the sign's geometry in 21\% of the edits, all edits are filtered by a geometric check and a manual review. Severity is measured as the LPIPS distance between the original and the edited sign plate. On 716 worn frames, we find that in detect-then-read pipelines, wear breaks detection before it breaks reading. The detector finds only 62\% of the worn signs, even though it finds every one of them in the original frames. Missed detections account for 78--87\% of failed reads, a pattern that a zero-shot detector shares. Given the annotated sign box, as in the crop-based benchmarks, a classifier still reads 78\% of the worn signs, but only 56\% when it has to rely on the detector

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用生成式图像编辑在真实街景限速标志上合成积雪、锈蚀、植被遮挡等六类磨损，构建成对原始的 ISA-Wear 数据集，并在 716 张磨损图上评估 detect-then-read 流水线的识别失效。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「磨损先破坏检测、再破坏读取」的失败归因（漏检占读取失败的 78–87%，给出裁剪框后分类精度仍达 78%）可作为核查 VLM 流水线中视觉证据在哪一环丢失的对照线索，但不涉及 latent 推理状态本身。
